{{recipe}}

A '''sticky date pudding''' is a favorite Australian pudding, especially in Southern climates in the winter months. Your family and friends will love you forever if you make them the following recipe.

==Ingredients==
=== Sauce ===

* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (480 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
* 1 cup (240 ml) water

=== Cake ===
*1 cup (240 ml) pitted [[Cookbook:Date|dates]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
*2 cups (480 ml) plain [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|bicarbonate of soda]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*2 tsp [[Cookbook:Mixed Spice|mixed spice]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], at room temperature
*1½ cups (360 ml) [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|castor sugar]]
*1 cup (240 ml) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
*2 tsp of [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] essence

=== Serving ===
*500 ml [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]]
 
==Equipment==
*[[Cookbook:Double Boiler|Double boiler]]
*Electric [[Cookbook:Mixer|mixer]] (a free standing one is better, as you need to beat the eggs for some time for best results)
*[[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]] or flour sifter
*Large [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake tin]], lined with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] and well-greased

==Procedure==

=== Sauce ===
# Place brown sugar and water in top of double boiler.
# Over simmering heat, stir until all brown sugar is dissolved.
# Remove from the heat, and set aside to cool.

=== Cake ===
# [[Cookbook:Chopping|Chop]] dates roughly, place in [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and add sodium bicarbonate along with just enough water to cover everything.
# Bring to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 1 minute. It should froth up from the bicarb; when it does, remove from heat once foam reaches the top of the saucepan.
# Set aside to cool.
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 180°C.
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] flour, bicarbonate of soda, salt, and mixed spice together twice.
# Beat eggs lightly. Add castor sugar and [[Cookbook:Whipping|whip]] as for making a sponge; it should be really light and fluffy.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] in oil and vanilla essence, but don’t over-mix this as you’ll lose all the air in the egg mixture.
# Fold in the sifted flour, sodium bicarbonate, and salt. Then, fold in the cooled date mixture.
# Pour into prepared tin. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in oven at 180°C for about 80–90 minutes, not too high in the oven or the top will burn. Cooking time and temperature can be reduced slightly if a fan-forced oven is used
# Test cake with [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]], which should come out dry. Remove from oven, and leave pudding in the tin

=== Serving ===
# Use a skewer to create lots of holes throughout the hot pudding
# Pour approximately 1 cup of caramel mixture onto the hot pudding; this will soak into the holes of the pudding
#Slice into desired portions, and serve immediately with cream or ice cream.
